summary:
On Fire is a web application that turns 25 years of NASA satellite fire detections into one consistent burning-activity calendar for the Middle East & North Africa and North America. NASA's MODIS (since 2000) and VIIRS (since 2012) sensors count fire very differently, so their records cannot be compared directly. We harmonize them: instead of raw hotspots we count "burning units" (a ~10 km square with fire on one day) and convert MODIS to the VIIRS scale with a model fitted per country and season. On years held out from fitting, this cut the disagreement between the two sensors from 144.1% to 30.3%.

Users pick any country, draw any area or type latitude/longitude, choose any date range, and see which months and years burn most, how this month compares with the historical median, and download the calendar (CSV, PNG) and every hotspot detected (CSV). For fires burning now, On Fire shows where they are heading, which towns they could reach and when, how big they are compared with past fires at the same place, and exports a CAP alert file for authorities. An AI fire-risk model, tested against what really burned, adds early warning.

It helps fire services, civil protection, scientists and land managers see what is normal for a place and act early when a season is not.
details: WHAT IT DOES 1. A harmonized burning-activity calendar for every country and both regions: 25 years month by month (amount or "compared to normal"), the fire season (the fewest months holding 75% of a year's fire), the worst month, the trend since 2001, the busiest years and months, and this month against the median of the same month. Hovering a month shows its burning units, its % of normal and the raw hotspots each sensor detected. 2. Any area of interest: draw a box on the map or type its latitude/longitude corners. The area gets its own 25-year calendar, extended to the latest satellite day, and "this month so far vs the same dates in 2012-2025" (median, middle half, rank). A box outside the covered countries is refused with a clear message instead of a false "no fire". 3. Any date range (Nov 2000 to yesterday): total burning, % of normal, busiest month, hotspots detected, a monthly chart, and downloads: monthly summary (CSV), every hotspot in the range (CSV, MODIS + VIIRS), calendar (CSV, PNG). 4. Live fires from five satellites (refreshed every 20 minutes, gas flares removed) on one map for both regions. 5. One fire: projected spread for +3/+6/+12/+24 h from the wind forecast, the first town it could reach and when, smoke, air quality, people nearby, emissions, its size compared with every fire within 50 km since 2012, and a CAP 1.2 alert file for authorities. Alerts are decision support labelled as estimates; the app never issues evacuation orders. 6. AI fire risk per ~50 km cell with the reasons behind each cell, and Truth vs Prediction, which replays past fires (Dixie, Kabylie, Manavgat 2021 and three chosen by rule) against the frozen model's earlier risk map, including its misses. HOW IT WORKS 1. Collect NASA FIRMS detections: MODIS Collection 6.1 (Nov 2000 - Dec 2025) and VIIRS S-NPP 375 m (Jan 2012 - Dec 2025) yearly country archives; 2026 and live data from the FIRMS API. 2. Clean both sensors the same way: vegetation fires only, a common confidence filter, static heat sources (gas flares, industry) removed. 3. Count the same thing: fire cell-days = distinct (0.1 degree cell, day) pairs with fire. This removes most of the pixel-size difference. 4. Calibrate MODIS to VIIRS on the 2012-2025 overlap per country and season (power law + small-fire background), chosen on inner validation years and scored only on held-out years 2014, 2017, 2020, 2023. 5. One record: VIIRS from 2012, calibrated MODIS before, with an uncertainty band; then calendar statistics (mean, median, anomalies, fire season). EVIDENCE - Disagreement between MODIS-derived and VIIRS monthly country totals on held-out years: 144.1% before, 30.3% after. At the 2012 sensor switch the harmonized series is off by a factor of 1.25 against MODIS alone; a naive switch is off by 6.5. - Gas flares: in Qatar 93.7% of VIIRS detections are static industrial sources; our detector agrees with NASA's static-source flag with 96.2% precision and 97.0% recall. - Risk model (LightGBM, trained to 2018, tuned 2019-2020, frozen, scored 2021-2025): 59.2% of 8,728 large fires began inside the model's top 10% of risk vs 47.8% for the fire map alone (assumes a perfect 7-day weather forecast). TRY IT (main task) On Windows, install Node.js and Python 3.11+, download the GitHub repository and double-click setup.bat. Click "Area", type North 37.2, South 35.5, West 3, East 9 (northern Algeria): you get "fires peak in August", the 25-year calendar, this month vs the median, and CSV downloads. TOOLS JavaScript, Python, HTML/CSS. React, Vite, MapLibre GL JS, Recharts, Node.js/Express, FastAPI/Uvicorn, DuckDB, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, LightGBM, Shapely, PyArrow. A standard Windows PC. WORKING NOW / LIMITS / FUTURE Working: everything above runs locally with setup.bat. Limits: prototype on the user's PC (no public hosting yet); values before 2012 are estimates (typically 0.58x-1.51x for a country-month); satellites miss fires under cloud; spread is a rule-of-thumb estimate; the risk model ranks places and cannot say where a fire starts; coverage is two regions. Future: extend to every region, add NOAA-20/21 VIIRS to the long record, public hosting for agencies.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS MODIS Collection 6.1 active fires (2000-2025 archive)
NASA FIRMS VIIRS 375 m active fires (S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21)
NASA FIRMS API (area, data availability, static-source flags)
NASA POWER weather data (fire-risk model training)
NASA GIBS VIIRS NOAA-20 corrected reflectance (satellite base map)
projectRefs: Open-Meteo forecast, archive and air-quality APIs (wind, fire weather, air quality; CC BY 4.0, CAMS)
OpenStreetMap via Overpass API (villages, buildings, roads, land use near a fire; ODbL)
GeoNames cities (town names and populations; CC BY 4.0)
Natural Earth boundaries and places (country/state borders, land outline; public domain)
Esri World Imagery and Boundaries & Places base maps (Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics; attributed on the map)
Open-source software: React, Vite, MapLibre GL JS, Recharts, Express, Turf, FastAPI, DuckDB, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, LightGBM, Shapely (full list in the README)
